patches.value: For every t>0, E(t)=∫_{R^n} e(x,t) dx. This is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral, used after spatial integrability has been established; there is no factor 1/2.

For every t>0, the density e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on R^n, E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. In particular E(t)=E(s) for all s,t>0. The density is |u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|^2 with Euclidean norms, and E(t) is its spatial Lebesgue integral, with no factor 1/2. No assertion at time zero is made.
